question: Can a direct runtime launch resolve a UID-backed autoload after the resource and its .uid sidecar were moved externally while .godot/uid_cache.bin still names the old path?

sources.title: Godot UID changes coming to 4.4
sources.claim: external file moves while the editor is closed are an explicit UID workflow goal; .uid sidecars should move with scripts/shaders

sources.title: Godot startup UID/autoload sequence
sources.claim: startup loads uid_cache.bin, fixes autoload UID paths immediately, and game startup later loads the resolved autoload path

distinguishing_outcomes: First runtime misses autoload at old path, editor/import scan repairs cache, second runtime loads moved autoload: retain stale-cache startup gap as a consequential external-move bug.
First runtime finds moved autoload immediately: another runtime UID discovery path handles stale existing cache entries; stop the hypothesis.
Editor/import scan also fails to repair cache: investigate scan lifecycle and fixture validity before widening the claim.
First runtime fails for reasons unrelated to autoload/UID resolution: repair fixture separately.
stop_condition: Capture first direct runtime, editor/import repair pass, and second direct runtime using one prepared stale-cache fixture.
